summary: Iteration 10: Validated per-user Gmail sync via Google Workspace DWD. Manager (yusuf@osagency.in) and team members (rupali, digital) can each independently sync their own Gmail inbox; data is scoped by owner_email across /api/inbox, /api/inbox/gmail-status, /api/inbox/sync, /api/inbox/clear-samples, /api/inbox/{id}/read, /api/inbox/parse-brief, /api/inbox/draft-reply. All critical frontend data-testids (inbox-detail, ai-create-brief, ai-draft-reply, brief-modal, create-job-btn, clear-samples-btn, inbox-item-{id}, gmail-status, sync-gmail-btn, inbox-page, inbox-list) are present and the Inbox UI works end-to-end on the public preview URL. 15/17 backend tests pass; 2 skipped due to intra-suite ordering (parallel class execution means TestClearSamples may wipe e-1 mocks before TestParseBrief/TestDraftReply classes run on another worker — product behaviour is correct). Credentials from /app/memory/test_credentials.md confirmed working: manager yusuf@osagency.in/manager123 and all team members with team123.

minor.issue: Mock inbox emails (e-1..e-5) are only re-seeded when the inbox collection is completely empty. Once Gmail sync has run (or clear-samples has been called), db.inbox.count_documents({})>0 keeps the mocks from being restored on backend restart. Not a per-user bug, but means AI Create Brief / Draft Reply demo for the mock emails is a one-shot. Consider gating the seed on a dedicated mock-count instead: db.inbox.count_documents({'source': {'$ne': 'gmail'}}) == 0.

action_items: (Minor) Tighten inbox seed re-population: gate on count of non-gmail docs so mock demo emails survive after a user clicks Clear samples or Sync Gmail. Current behaviour means after first sync, e-1..e-5 are gone permanently on this environment.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 2837 lines — approaching the 'should be split' threshold; consider breaking inbox/gmail/auth routers into separate modules.

test_credentials.md and the LoginPage HINTS array both duplicate the seed account list; drift-prone. A /api/demo-accounts endpoint (or import from seed_data) would eliminate repeated iteration-7/8/9 breakage.
Mock inbox seed gating logic (seed_data.py:217) is incorrect for a long-running environment where Gmail sync fills the collection — the mocks silently never come back.
